Class EntityLimitJpaRepositoryImpl

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.repository.BaseRepositoryImpl<EntityLimit>
grafiosch.repository.EntityLimitJpaRepositoryImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
BaseRepositoryCustom<EntityLimit>, EntityLimitJpaRepositoryCustom
public class EntityLimitJpaRepositoryImpl extends BaseRepositoryImpl<EntityLimit> implements EntityLimitJpaRepositoryCustom
Custom repository operations for EntityLimit: validating a row against the limit key catalogue before it is written, and producing the key definitions the administration UI offers.

    • saveOnlyAttributes

      public EntityLimit saveOnlyAttributes(EntityLimit entityLimit, EntityLimit existingEntity, Set<Class<? extends Annotation>> updatePropertyLevelClasses) throws Exception
      Description copied from interface: BaseRepositoryCustom
      Saves only specific attributes of an entity based on property-level update permissions. Uses annotation-based access control to determine which fields can be modified by the current user.
      Specified by:
      saveOnlyAttributes in interface BaseRepositoryCustom<EntityLimit>
      Parameters:
      entityLimit - the entity containing the new values to be saved
      existingEntity - the current entity from the database, null for new entities
      updatePropertyLevelClasses - set of annotation classes that define update permission levels
      Returns:
      the saved entity with updated attributes
      Throws:
      Exception - if the save operation fails, validation errors occur, or security constraints are violated

    • getLimitKeyDefinitions

      @Transactional public List<LimitKeyDefinition> getLimitKeyDefinitions(Integer idUser, Integer idEntityLimit)
      Description copied from interface: EntityLimitJpaRepositoryCustom
      Returns every limit key an administrator may configure, as the definitions the edit form needs.

      Two halves are unioned. The registered MAX keys come from the limit key registry with their counter's scopes, their fresh-install default, their validation rule and their message key. The DAY_CUD and DAY_READ keys are derived: every concrete, non-abstract Auditable entity that is not an AdminEntity, taken from the JPA metamodel, plus the registered pseudo entity names. Deriving them means an administrator keeps exactly the reach they have today, including entities that have no configured default at all.

      Keys for which the given user already holds a row are filtered out, so the picker cannot produce a duplicate.

      Specified by:
      getLimitKeyDefinitions in interface EntityLimitJpaRepositoryCustom
      Parameters:
      idUser - the user the new or edited row belongs to, or null for a row that is not user-scoped
      idEntityLimit - the row currently being edited, whose own key must stay in the list, or null on create
      Returns:
      the offered key definitions, registered MAX keys first
